description: The openseek session transcript (`openseek_session-<id>.jsonl`): the first line is a SessionFileHeader and every later line a SessionEvent. This schema is the source of truth for the on-disk format. The session types in agent_session (session_types.mbt) and the header record in agent_session/log (header_record.mbt) are generated from it; see `just gen-session-types`.

SessionFileHeader.description: The header record on the first line of a session file: the session identity and system prompt for the event lines that follow.

version.description: The session file format version; this build reads version 1.

SessionEvent.description:
One append-only event in a session log.

Sequence numbers are one-based within a session and are assigned by `Session::append_event`. The durable store rejects non-contiguous sequences when loading from disk.

sequence.description: One-based position in the session log.

ts.description: Wall-clock stamp (unix milliseconds) of when the event was appended; 0 for purely in-memory sessions appended without a clock (the durable store always stamps).

oneOf.description: User-authored model input, including the initial task and any steering text. JSON tag: `user`. Projection replays it as a user-role message.

Model output for one response. JSON tag: `assistant`. Projection preserves visible content, optional reasoning content, and native DeepSeek tool calls; those tool calls open pending ids that later `Tool` events may answer.

Local result for one assistant tool call. JSON tag: `tool_result`. Projection emits it only when `tool_call_id` matches a pending assistant call; unmatched results are ignored to keep model replay protocol-valid.
Runtime-injected context, such as a plan reminder. JSON tag: `runtime_notice`. Projection sends it as a user-role message even though it did not originate from the user's prompt.

Append-only compaction metadata for an inclusive event sequence range. JSON tag: `summary`. Projection skips covered earlier events when a later summary covers their sequence and emits the summary text instead.
Completion status for an agent turn. JSON tag: `terminal`. `Finished(text)` can project as a final assistant message; aborted, interrupted, and failed terminals project assistant status messages.

SessionItem.description:
Payload vocabulary for one `SessionEvent`.

`User` and `Runtime` project as user-role model messages. `Assistant` projects as an assistant message and may open pending tool calls. `Tool` answers a pending assistant tool call. `Summary` is append-only compaction metadata that can replace older events during projection. `Terminal` records turn completion status and may project as a final assistant/status message.

submission_id.description: The submitting controller's tag for this input, echoed from a serve `prompt` or `steer` command so a delivery can be reconciled by exact id rather than by matching text (two clients can submit identical text into one session). Absent for untagged input, including TUI and one-shot prompts, and older records without a tag.

UserMessage.description:
User-authored model input for one conversational event.

A `UserMessage` is durable data, not a UI transcript item. It records the ordered content that should be replayed as a user-role message in `Session::chat_messages`.

arguments.description: The raw JSON argument string from the model.

SessionToolCall.description: One tool call requested by the model, kept durable so later `ToolResult` events can match its id.

is_replay.description: True only when a checkpoint re-appends an answer that an earlier durable provider step already owns. Absent on ordinary messages.

usage.description: The provider response's token usage, on the first durable record of that response only. Absent on replays and on logs written before it existed.

AssistantMessage.description:
Assistant output returned by the model for one event.

This stores visible assistant text, requested tool calls, and optional reasoning content. Tool calls are durable because later `ToolResult` events must match their call ids during `Session::chat_messages` projection.

brief.description: An optional one-line, human-readable summary of what the call did (e.g. `ran ls → 12 files`), for display only; never replayed to the model.

data.description: Machine-readable output and nested PTC trace, excluded from model projection.

ToolResult.description:
Result returned by a local tool for one assistant tool call.

During model projection, a `ToolResult` is emitted only when its `tool_call_id` matches a pending assistant tool call. Unmatched results are ignored to keep replay protocol-valid.

RuntimeNotice.description:
Out-of-band runtime notice surfaced to the model.

Runtime notices are projected as user-role messages. They are intended for loop-injected context such as plan reminders or other text that did not originate from the user's prompt.

SessionSummary.description:
Durable compaction record for older session events.

A summary does not delete the covered raw events. It records that `from_sequence..to_sequence` can be replaced by `content` when projecting model context. The durable event log remains append-only.

TurnTerminal.description: How a turn ended. `message` is absent only for `max_steps_exhausted`; `verbatim` marks a message that must not be reinterpreted by the legacy rules (a `finished` message starting with the context-yield prefix, a `failed` message equal to the max-steps text).

Content.description: Message content: a plain string for a single text part (the original format), otherwise an array of parts.

TokenUsage.description: Token counts for one provider response, as its durable `AssistantMessage` records them. The fields and JSON match the `usage` event, so a reader of the session log can account for a run without its event stream: summed over a turn's messages, they equal the turn's `usage` events.
